title: ANY.RUN describes five Thanksgiving and Black Friday phishing and malware campaigns seen in 2026
date_note: Publication day of the ANY.RUN blog post; the campaigns it describes were observed between September and November 2026.
place: ANY.RUN (location not stated in the source)
geo_basis: no place stated in the source
summary: ANY.RUN's blog post describes five holiday-themed campaigns it observed: a fake Thanksgiving invitation leading to a Google Workspace login page, an e-card that downloads a ScreenConnect installer, a fake MyChart survey collecting personal data, a Black Friday newsletter hiding an NDA phishing link, and a Word coupon with an embedded VBS script. ANY.RUN says the script's download failed in all observed tasks.
plain: Security firm ANY.RUN lists five holiday-themed scams and malware lures it saw this autumn, from fake logins to a fake coupon document.
exec: ANY.RUN reports holiday-themed lures aimed at employees and shoppers, including a credential-theft page and a remote-access installer.
action: ANY.RUN advises investigating what happens after a user clicks a link or opens a file, monitoring for unauthorized remote-management installs, and watching for Office-to-script process chains such as WINWORD.EXE to wscript.exe to schtasks.exe.

validation.note: Only the ANY.RUN post itself was read.

review.note: Compared five campaigns, VBS failure, date, severity against ANY.RUN post

key_findings: ANY.RUN describes five holiday-themed campaigns: a fake Google Workspace login, a ScreenConnect installer delivered via a fake e-card PDF, a fake MyChart survey, an NDA phishing link inside a genuine newsletter, and a coupon document with an embedded VBS script.
It says the Google Workspace phishing operation had been active since August 2026.
For the ScreenConnect case it says intended victims and follow-on activity were not confirmed.
It says the VBS script attempted a second-stage download and a scheduled task, but the download failed in all nine observed tasks.
recommendations: Investigate what happens after a user clicks a link or opens a file, not just the email itself.
Monitor for unauthorized remote-management installs and unexpected PDF-to-browser transitions.
Watch for Office-to-script process chains such as WINWORD.EXE to wscript.exe to schtasks.exe.
Inspect image-only emails and trace traffic distribution system redirect chains.
